What Is It Good for? | Kashish Parpiani Kashish Parpiani joins host Tushar Shetty to examine whether the Quad still matters as its leaders reconvene after two years.

From left: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in a Quad leader family photo at the Solaire Resort in Manila, Philippines at the ASEAN Summit, Nov. 17, 2026.

Kashish Parpiani, co-author of “America and the Indo-Pacific: Trump and Beyond” and a member of the Council on Foreign Relations’ Emerging Leaders in Business and Geopolitics program, joins host Tushar Shetty to examine whether the Quad still matters as its leaders reconvene after two years.

They discuss the Quad’s origins and its rejection of the “Asian NATO” label, why 2026 has been a productive year despite the delayed leaders’ summit, the Quad’s complementary role alongside ASEAN, the Critical Minerals Framework and China’s catch-22 in weaponizing supply chains, India’s multivector diplomacy across the Quad, SCO and BRICS, and how a Democrat-led Congress and a possible G3 order could shape the grouping’s future.
Tushar Shetty is an Economist-in-training at HTW Berlin and host of the Beyond the Indus podcast.
